issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires continuous target search as an ongoing activity (do) in the operating state. The binding hints provide all three S4 inputs (state=TargetSearch, phase=do, action=target search). The closed model has no actions declared, so the required do-activity is missing from the carrier state.

issues.basis: NL2 segment; verify_fact reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 refuted; inspection_fact STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL refs=[state:TargetSearch:line:7]; FCSTM transition:line:21 ([*]→InitialState) as sole root initial; FCSTM transition:line:9 ([*]→TargetSearch) exists within Region1 but Region1 itself is unreachable; PlantUML -- separator at line 5 establishing concurrent region boundary
issues.expected: The TargetSearch state must be reachable from the model root so the UAV can enter its target-search operating mode and perform the continuous search activity required by NL2.
issues.observed: The verify fact reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 is refuted (reachable_from_initial=false). The root's only top-level initial edge is transition:line:21 ([*]→InitialState), which enters region 0. No edge from InitialState or the root enters Region1 where TargetSearch resides. The inspection facts confirm 6 of 8 states are unreachable, including all Region1 and Region2 members.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the UAV to actively perform target search in the TargetSearch state. The deterministic verify facts confirm TargetSearch is unreachable from the model's initial entry. The root cause is that the PlantUML concurrent region structure (-- separators) is not reflected in the FCSTM's reachability topology: the root initial edge only activates region 0 (InitialState), leaving regions 1 and 2 (containing all operational states) inaccessible. This derived contract captures the independently required reachability of the NL2 operating state.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML -- separators establish concurrent region semantics, under which all regions (including Region1) would be entered simultaneously when the root is active. If the FCSTM correctly implemented concurrent region entry, TargetSearch would be reachable via Region1's internal initial edge (transition:line:9). The structural defect is in the FCSTM's failure to activate concurrent regions from the root entry, not in the absence of an internal initial edge.
issues.title: TargetSearch operating state unreachable from model root initial entry

issues.basis: NL4 segment; verify_fact reachability:state:AttackReady:line:14 refuted; inspection_fact STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL refs=[state:AttackReady:line:14]; FCSTM transition:line:21 as sole root initial; FCSTM transition:line:16 ([*]→AttackReady) exists within Region2 but Region2 is unreachable; PlantUML -- separator at line 17 establishing concurrent region boundary; semantic binding BIND-NL4-SOURCE-ATTACKREADY
issues.expected: The AttackReady state (the 'flight state' where the UAV awaits task assignment) must be reachable from the model root so the UAV can be in its operational flight mode when task assignment information arrives.
issues.observed: The verify fact reachability:state:AttackReady:line:14 is refuted (reachable_from_initial=false). The root's only top-level initial edge targets InitialState in region 0. No edge enters Region2 where AttackReady resides. The inspection facts confirm AttackReady and all Region2 members are unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: NL4 requires the UAV to be 'during flight' (AttackReady) as the precondition for receiving task assignment. The deterministic verify facts confirm AttackReady is unreachable from the model's initial entry. This is an independently required operating scope from the NL2 reachability: it belongs to a different concurrent region (Region2) and serves a different NL obligation (attack entry vs. target search). The same root-cause structural defect (concurrent regions not activated) affects both, but the obligations are semantically distinct and require separate contracts.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state. After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: As with TargetSearch, the PlantUML concurrent region semantics would activate Region2 simultaneously with the root entry, making AttackReady reachable via Region2's internal initial edge (transition:line:16). The defect is the FCSTM's failure to model concurrent region activation, not the absence of an internal entry edge.
issues.title: AttackReady flight state unreachable from model root initial entry

issues.basis: NL4 'the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly'; FCSTM transition:line:18 effects=[]; reference_inspection_facts variables count=0, var_dataflow count=0; FCSTM model declares no variables; event name 'Attack_Complete_UAV_Count_Decreased' is an identifier, not a variable_delta effect
issues.expected: After the Attack to AttackReady transition (attack completion), a variable representing the UAV count must decrease, formalized as a variable_delta effect on the transition or an equivalent dataflow in the closed model
locus_names: number of UAVs in the swarm
issues.observed: The closed model declares zero variables (variables count=0, var_dataflow count=0); the transition Attack to AttackReady (transition:line:18) has effects=[]; no variable or dataflow exists to represent or modify the UAV count
issues.reason: NL4 explicitly requires a variable delta: 'the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.' This is a data modification obligation that requires a declared variable and an effect. The closed model has no variables and no effects on any transition. The event name mentions the decrease but does not constitute a formal variable_delta in the executable model. No frozen predicate covers variable_delta, so this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event name 'Attack_Complete_UAV_Count_Decreased' and the PlantUML label 'Attack Complete / UAV Count Decreased' encode the semantic content of the decrease in their identifiers; one could argue the effect is captured at the event-naming level rather than requiring a separate variable declaration. However, the NL explicitly states 'the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases' as a state change to a quantified variable, which requires formal variable tracking in the model
issues.title: Missing variable delta for UAV count decrease after attack completion

issues.basis: NL2 'continuously performs target search tasks'; verify_facts reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 status=refuted, reachability:state:Region1:line:6 status=refuted; inspection_equivalent_facts LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at InitialState (line 20, outgoing_count=0); FCSTM transition:line:21 is the only root initial edge targeting InitialState; FCSTM transition:line:9 is Region1-internal [*] to TargetSearch with no root-level path to Region1; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_refs=[root, InitialState] only
issues.expected: The TargetSearch state (and its enclosing Region1 composite) must be reachable from the root initial entry so the UAV can operationally perform target search as required by the continuous operation obligation
issues.observed: Verify facts show reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 refuted and reachability:state:Region1:line:6 refuted; the root's only initial edge (transition:line:21) targets InitialState in region 0; InitialState is a reachable dead leaf with zero outgoing transitions; Region1 has an internal initial edge (transition:line:9) to TargetSearch but no root-level entry to Region1 itself; inspection facts confirm 6 unreachable states including all of Region1 and Region2
issues.reason: The NL requires the UAV to 'continuously perform target search tasks,' establishing an operational availability obligation for the target search state. The cross-view grounding reveals that in the closed FCSTM model, the target search state is unreachable from the root initial entry. The root only activates InitialState (region 0), which is a dead leaf. While the PlantUML source uses concurrent region syntax that in standard UML would activate all regions simultaneously, the FCSTM reachability analysis (which is the authoritative closed-model fact) shows these regions are not reached. This is a behavioral consequence: the system cannot perform target search because it cannot reach the state where target search occurs.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: In UML concurrent region semantics, all regions of a composite state are simultaneously active upon entry to the composite; the PlantUML source shows Region1 with its own [*] to TargetSearch initial edge, which in standard UML means Region1 should be entered when the root composite is entered. The FCSTM reachability analysis may be applying sequential reachability to a concurrent structure, and the concurrent region annotation in the FCSTM text confirms the intended parallelism. If concurrent entry semantics are correctly applied, Region1 and its children would be reachable upon root activation.
issues.title: Target search operating scope unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: NL3 'When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state'; verify_facts event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers[0] consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:10] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; transition:line:10 source state TargetSearch is unreachable per verify_facts reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 refuted
issues.expected: The Interception_Detected event must have at least one reachable consumer transition in the target search operating scope so the interception response can be operationally triggered when the event occurs at runtime
issues.observed: Verify facts show event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted; inspection facts show the event has one declared consumer (transition:line:10, TargetSearch to FormationAdjustment) but zero reachable consumer transitions; the consumer state TargetSearch is unreachable from root initial, so the event cannot be operationally consumed
issues.reason: NL3 requires an operational response to interception. While the consumer transition exists and is correctly wired (satisfying the endpoint contract), the consumer state is unreachable, making the event operationally unconsumable. This is a distinct property from endpoint existence: the event can be declared and the transition can be present, but if no reachable state can consume the event, the NL obligation 'When intercepted, transitions to formation adjustment' cannot be fulfilled at runtime. No frozen predicate directly covers event_consumer_coverage, so this remains predicate-null W1.
issues.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event consumer is correctly declared and wired: transition:line:10 has the correct source (TargetSearch), target (FormationAdjustment), and trigger (Interception_Detected). The wiring satisfies the NL3 endpoint contract. The unreachability is an upstream structural issue (root does not enter Region1) rather than a consumer coverage defect per se; if concurrent region entry semantics are applied, the consumer would become reachable. The consumer coverage failure is derivative of the reachability failure.
issues.title: Interception event has no reachable consumer in the target search operating scope

semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2 requires the UAV swarm to 'continuously perform target search tasks.' The G1 predicate (may_reach) completed with verdict=false on the closed FCSTM input, confirming no finite path exists from the root initial entry (InitialState) to TargetSearch within Region1. The receipt counterexample explicitly shows sources=[InitialState] and targets=[Region1.TargetSearch] with no trace path. The root's only top-level initial edge (transition:line:21) enters region 0 only. Region1's internal initial edge (transition:line:9) exists but is unreachable because no root-level edge enters Region1. The obligation's evidence catalog does not include the PlantUML -- separator line that would support a concurrent-region alternative reading, so no catalog-backed undercutting defeater survives.

The receipt counterexample shows sources=[InitialState] and targets=[Region1.TargetSearch]. The violation is established in the closed model; the concurrent region reading is a surviving undercutting alternative supported by exact catalog evidence.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The PlantUML source at line 5 uses a -- separator establishing concurrent region semantics, under which all regions of the root composite (including Region1) would be simultaneously activated upon root entry. If the FCSTM correctly projected this concurrent structure, Region1 and TargetSearch would be reachable via Region1's internal initial edge (transition:line:9). The FCSTM's sequential topology may be a projection artifact of the concurrent source structure rather than a fundamental absence of intended connectivity.

candidates.observed: Verify facts show reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 refuted and reachability:state:Region1:line:6 refuted; the root's only initial edge (transition:line:21) targets InitialState in region 0; InitialState is a reachable dead leaf with zero outgoing transitions; Region1 has an internal initial edge (transition:line:9) to TargetSearch but no root-level entry to Region1 itself; inspection facts confirm 6 unreachable states including all of Region1 and Region2
candidates.reason: The NL requires the UAV to 'continuously perform target search tasks,' establishing an operational availability obligation for the target search state. The cross-view grounding reveals that in the closed FCSTM model, the target search state is unreachable from the root initial entry. The root only activates InitialState (region 0), which is a dead leaf. While the PlantUML source uses concurrent region syntax that in standard UML would activate all regions simultaneously, the FCSTM reachability analysis (which is the authoritative closed-model fact) shows these regions are not reached. This is a behavioral consequence: the system cannot perform target search because it cannot reach the state where target search occurs.
candidates.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: In UML concurrent region semantics, all regions of a composite state are simultaneously active upon entry to the composite; the PlantUML source shows Region1 with its own [*] to TargetSearch initial edge, which in standard UML means Region1 should be entered when the root composite is entered. The FCSTM reachability analysis may be applying sequential reachability to a concurrent structure, and the concurrent region annotation in the FCSTM text confirms the intended parallelism. If concurrent entry semantics are correctly applied, Region1 and its children would be reachable upon root activation.

candidate.basis: NL3 'When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state'; verify_facts event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers[0] consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:10] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; transition:line:10 source state TargetSearch is unreachable per verify_facts reachability:state:TargetSearch:line:7 refuted
candidate.expected: The Interception_Detected event must have at least one reachable consumer transition in the target search operating scope so the interception response can be operationally triggered when the event occurs at runtime
candidate.observed: Verify facts show event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted; inspection facts show the event has one declared consumer (transition:line:10, TargetSearch to FormationAdjustment) but zero reachable consumer transitions; the consumer state TargetSearch is unreachable from root initial, so the event cannot be operationally consumed
candidate.reason: NL3 requires an operational response to interception. While the consumer transition exists and is correctly wired (satisfying the endpoint contract), the consumer state is unreachable, making the event operationally unconsumable. This is a distinct property from endpoint existence: the event can be declared and the transition can be present, but if no reachable state can consume the event, the NL obligation 'When intercepted, transitions to formation adjustment' cannot be fulfilled at runtime. No frozen predicate directly covers event_consumer_coverage, so this remains predicate-null W1.
candidate.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
candidate.strongest_rebuttal: The event consumer is correctly declared and wired: transition:line:10 has the correct source (TargetSearch), target (FormationAdjustment), and trigger (Interception_Detected). The wiring satisfies the NL3 endpoint contract. The unreachability is an upstream structural issue (root does not enter Region1) rather than a consumer coverage defect per se; if concurrent region entry semantics are applied, the consumer would become reachable. The consumer coverage failure is derivative of the reachability failure.
candidate.title: Interception event has no reachable consumer in the target search operating scope
